skill.name: ai-video-generation
skill.description: Generate AI video workflows with inference.sh models, including text-to-video, image-to-video, avatar, lipsync, foley, and upscaling examples.
skill.summary: Use inference.sh video models through the belt CLI for prompt, image, avatar, and editing workflows.
skill.author: halt-catch-fire

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, model identifiers, code fences, and example URLs. No prompt injection attempt or covert exfiltration language was found in SKILL.md. Residual risk comes from expected third-party CLI processing and unpinned external skill installation guidance.

remediation.issue: Third-party media processing is central to the workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear privacy note that prompts, URLs, images, audio, and video may be sent to inference.sh and model providers.

remediation.issue: External skill installation commands are not pinned to immutable reviewed versions.
remediation.suggestion: Pin recommended skills to reviewed versions or commits, and ask users to verify source before installing related skills.

remediation.issue: Markdown backticks around identifiers create noisy static command findings.
remediation.suggestion: Use plain text or tables for model identifiers when possible, and keep executable examples in clearly labeled command blocks.

semantic_findings.title: Third-Party CLI Video Processing
semantic_findings.description: The skill grants Bash access for belt commands and directs users to run hosted inference.sh video apps. Prompts and media URLs can be sent to third-party services during normal use.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The allowed tool declaration and examples clearly center on belt app run calls to hosted video models. This is expected functionality, but it creates privacy and cost exposure.

content.user_title: Create AI Videos with Inference.sh Models
content.value_statement: Teams need fast ways to turn prompts, images, and audio into video assets. This skill provides model choices and CLI examples for inference.sh video workflows.
actual_capabilities: Lists text-to-video models such as Google Veo, Grok Video, Seedance, HappyHorse, Wan, and P-Video.
Shows image-to-video workflows for Wan, Seedance, HappyHorse, and P-Video.
Provides avatar, lipsync, foley, upscaling, and media merge examples.
Gives belt app run patterns for prompts, images, audio, videos, and reference images.
Links to inference.sh documentation for running apps and streaming results.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh belt CLI and an authenticated account.
Generated quality, speed, cost, and availability depend on external model providers.
User media URLs and prompts may be sent to third-party services.
The skill provides examples, not a local video rendering engine.

use_cases.title: Social Video Creation
use_cases.description: Create short clips from prompts or images for posts, ads, and campaign tests.

use_cases.title: Product Demo Drafting
use_cases.description: Generate concept videos, product reveal shots, and explainer clips before production.

use_cases.title: Media Pipeline Prototyping
use_cases.description: Combine video generation, foley, upscaling, and merging into repeatable workflow plans.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Text Video
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a short text-to-video request for [subject] using a fast model. Include duration, style, and a concise prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Animate an Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me animate this image URL with gentle camera movement: [url]. Recommend a model and describe the needed input fields.

prompt_templates.title: Talking Head Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a talking-head video using this portrait and audio. Select a lipsync or avatar model and list privacy checks before running it.

prompt_templates.title: Full Video Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an inference.sh video workflow that generates clips, adds foley, upscales the result, and merges the final sequence. Include model choices and checkpoints.

output_examples.input: Create a five-second product reveal video from a text prompt.
output_examples.output: Recommended Google Veo 3.1 Fast. The plan defines product material, camera movement, lighting, duration, and optional audio.

output_examples.input: Animate a portrait with an audio narration.
output_examples.output: Recommended Fabric or PixVerse Lipsync. The plan covers portrait URL, audio URL, consent checks, and the expected talking-head result.

output_examples.input: Improve a silent clip for social media.
output_examples.output: Recommended foley generation, upscaling, and a final merge step. The plan checks clip length, sound prompt, resolution, and export needs.

best_practices: Confirm you have rights and consent for every image, voice, and video source.
Use non-sensitive URLs and prompts because media can be processed by external providers.
Start with short, low-cost clips before running long or high-resolution jobs.
anti_patterns: Do not submit private faces, voices, or customer media without approval.
Do not assume every model supports the same duration, resolution, or audio options.
Do not run broad automation without checking inference costs and provider terms.

faq.question: Does this skill generate videos locally?
faq.answer: No. It guides the belt CLI, which runs hosted inference.sh video apps.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Do I need an account?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples require the inference.sh belt CLI and login.

faq.question: Can it animate images?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes image-to-video and reference-to-video examples.

faq.question: Can it make talking-head videos?
faq.answer: Yes. It lists avatar and lipsync models for portrait and audio inputs.

faq.question: Should I use sensitive media?
faq.answer: No. Treat prompts, URLs, images, audio, and videos as data sent to external services.
